claims.text: Opinion: the top frame is where the failure was detected, and the topmost frame naming a file of your own repository is usually where it was caused, because that is the last point at which your code chose what to pass.

Opinion: read the exception type and message in full before searching the web, because they are the narrowest description of the failure available; the type names the kind of failure and the message is written by whoever wrote the check.
Opinion: an inner exception is worth carrying because the wrapper says what the program was attempting while the inner one says what went wrong; either alone leaves out half of the diagnosis.
Opinion: reading only the outer trace of this sample sends you to line 30, which is correct reporting code, so the inner trace is the half that names the failing call (line 26).
claims.source_hint: examples/don-hang at stage-0: ThrowsDeep.cs lines 26 and 30 against the captured output

claims.text: A frame reads `at <namespace>.<type>.<method>(<parameter types and names>)`, followed by ` in <file>:line <n>` only for code built with debugging information — `System.Int32.Parse(String s)` shows none. Parameter types are the runtime's: `int` prints as `Int32`, `string?` as `String`.

claims.text: An exception's stack trace records the frames from the throw site up to the frame that handles it, so its bottom line is the outermost call still recorded — in this sample Run, which catches the exception — not necessarily where the program started.
